name: machine hands kept on one target: installing, teaching and updating every runner
what_it_changes: P14 says the room adjusts its machine hands. In these rooms the adjusting is a step of its own: members install the script and teach it, and they keep every runner's target current, because a stale target undoes the room's own new design. A revision must reach the operator and the target file, not only the people.
why: Cut rules R1 and R2 (tree-D4.md), with R1a (the level): the key's lines, read whole in _analysis/d4a02_keys/add-step_P14_T3-028.txt, state one shared change to P14. R1a: T3-028 (running scripts for the work) holds 50 of the 58 rooms. 'Synchronizing script versions and coordinates prevents outdated targets ... from wasting placements by repairing one another' (AmericanFlaginPlace); 'Friendly alterations require disabling or retargeting active repair scripts rather than only telling humans about a new plan' (teslamotors); 'A proposed revision must reach the operator and be encoded in the target before automated upkeep stops undoing it' (zootopia). These are the labelers' how sentences.
